clue.text: Blue-blooded members of a family of 6

definitions.text: Blue-blooded members of a family of 6

parts.words: Blue-blooded members of a family of 6
parts.note: reads as aristocrats of a noble house, but 6 down is a wild plant and this is the folk name of one member of its family

explanation.surface: A description of the titled members of some aristocratic household.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 down is ARUM; the wild arum (cuckoo-pint) is popularly called by the same name as a gathering of peers and their wives.
explanation.definitionFit: Peers and peeresses are the blue-blooded nobility, and the wild cuckoo-pint plant carries that folk name.

clue.text: Written order for 21 down requiring a little more time

definitions.text: Written order for 21 down requiring a little more time

parts.words: Written order for 21 down requiring a little more time
parts.note: a tempo marking printed on a score, asking for a pace rather slow, a shade quicker than the broadest slow marking

explanation.surface: An instruction on a score asking the players to take things a bit slower.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 down is MUSIC. The Italian marking is a diminutive of largo, so it asks for slightly less slowness than largo itself.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian tempo direction tells players to perform fairly slowly, a little faster than largo.

clue.text: Smoother in verse!

parts.note: run 'in verse' together and it becomes 'inverse': the opposite of smoother

explanation.surface: A remark that poetry makes things run more smoothly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in verse' looks like a reference to poetry, but read as one word it is 'inverse', asking for the opposite of smoother.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of a smoother texture is a coarser, more uneven one.

clue.text: Splash with the Scotch

parts.note: a splash is the small dash of fizzy mixer added to a glass of whisky

explanation.surface: Asking for a splash of something in a whisky.
explanation.walkthrough: Scotch is whisky; 'whisky and a splash' is the classic bar order with fizzy water.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbonated water is the mixer traditionally splashed into a whisky.

clue.text: See 1
My boy's Dutch

parts.note: in Cockney slang 'my old Dutch' is a wife, so this is the wife of my son

explanation.surface: Someone noting that their son is Dutch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dutch' looks like a nationality, but Cockney 'my old Dutch' (from duchess) means one's wife; a son's wife is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A son's wife is related to his parents by marriage, the female in-law of the next generation.

clue.text: A very odd bloomer

parts.note: rum is an old British word for strange or very odd

explanation.surface: Someone describing a peculiar flower, or a peculiar mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' suggests a blunder, but here it is a plant that blooms.
explanation.definitionFit: The arum lily is a flowering plant, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Injures 999 couples

parts.note: in Roman numerals I before M is one less than a thousand
couples are pairs

explanation.surface: An emergency call about two couples who have been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 999 is the British emergency number, but here it is the Roman numeral IM (one taken from a thousand).
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or weaken something is to harm it, the same as injuring it.

clue.text: A self-important walk for a : mere prop

definitions.meaning: a structural bar that simply supports a frame

explanation.surface: A swagger that is really only holding someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A swagger is a proud walk, and a brace is a supporting rod in a framework.

clue.text: Make a collection on the hoof

definitions.text: Make a collection on the hoof

parts.words: Make a collection on the hoof
parts.note: 'on the hoof' sounds like doing something hurriedly, but here it means livestock: gathering cattle together

explanation.surface: Collecting donations hurriedly, without planning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the hoof' usually means improvised; here it is literal, cattle being herded together by cowboys.
explanation.definitionFit: Ranchers gather scattered cattle into a herd in a drive of this name.

clue.text: Top teacher's appointment given bad press, poor fish!

indicators.note: bad suggests the letters of the following words are spoiled and must be reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An academic whose appointment got a hostile reception in the newspapers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bad' rearranges PRESS POOR FISH; 'given' only links. 'press' looks like the newspapers but is anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A university chair is the senior teaching post an academic holds.

clue.text: He may hold the post after snatching it from another

definitions.text: He may hold the post after snatching it from another

parts.words: He may hold the post after snatching it from another
parts.note: someone who seizes a position, throne or office wrongfully from its rightful holder

explanation.surface: A job-holder who got the position by grabbing it from a rival.
explanation.definitionFit: One who seizes power or a throne without the right to it is a pretender who grabbed it.

clue.text: Ditched fencing with some mirth?

definitions.meaning: a sunken fence set in a ditch so it does not spoil the view from a country house

explanation.surface: A fence with a ditch that someone finds amusing.
explanation.walkthrough: A ha-ha is a boundary sunk in a ditch on English country estates, keeping livestock out without blocking the view.
explanation.definitionFit: A sunken garden boundary bears the name, and so does written laughter.

clue.text: Health official taking tea or coffee

parts.note: MO is a medical officer
cha is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A medical officer having a hot drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'or' only link; tea looks like a choice offered beside coffee but is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong coffee named after a Yemeni port, often mixed with chocolate.

clue.text: Unhappily tied to controlled intake…

indicators.note: unhappily says the letters of the next word are in a sorry, disordered state

explanation.surface: Someone miserably tied to a regime of restricted eating.
explanation.definitionFit: A regime limiting what one eats is a regulated consumption of food.

clue.text: Plans of Wales bound to help the traveller

definitions.text: Plans of Wales bound to help the traveller

parts.words: Plans of Wales bound to help the traveller
parts.note: maps of the principality bound together in a book for travellers

explanation.surface: Schemes for Wales that are certain to assist tourists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plans' looks like schemes and 'bound to' like 'sure to', but they are maps and a bound book.
explanation.definitionFit: A book of maps covering Wales serves a traveller in finding the way.

clue.text: See 15
… but being over 21, nine reduced fractionally

definitions.text: but being over 21, nine reduced fractionally

parts.words: but being over 21, nine reduced fractionally
parts.note: nine placed over twenty-one makes a fraction, and cancelling by three reduces it

explanation.surface: A continuation about dieting: someone past 21 who has slimmed down a bit.
explanation.walkthrough: It continues 14 across. 'over 21' looks like age, but nine over 21 is a fraction; dividing top and bottom by three gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Nine twenty-firsts in lowest terms becomes a fraction of three parts in seven.

clue.text: Not hanging smoothly like the blossoms in the market, place

definitions.meaning: creased or gathered in folds, said of cloth

definitions.text: like the blossoms in the market, place
definitions.meaning: flowers on a market stall tied together in bunches

explanation.surface: A badly fitting garment beside a flower stall in a market square.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric gathered in folds hangs badly, and cut flowers on a stall are tied in clusters.

clue.text: Breathtaking despatch-of 11, perhaps?

parts.note: breathtaking taken literally: killing off the usurper of 11 across, the fate a usurper risks

explanation.surface: A stunning dispatch about a usurper.
explanation.walkthrough: 11 across is USURPER. 'Breathtaking' looks like amazing, but means literally taking breath away, killing; 'despatch' is killing too.
explanation.definitionFit: Murdering a political figure such as a usurping ruler is a political killing.

clue.text: A great trouble for the lady's maid

parts.note: great means big
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: A big problem for a household servant.
explanation.walkthrough: An abigail is an old literary word for a lady's personal maid, after a servant in the Bible and a stage play.
explanation.definitionFit: Named after a waiting woman in the Bible, this is a dated word for a female attendant.

clue.text: Order to take off a tie Tim knotted

indicators.note: knotted says the letters are tangled up and must be untangled

explanation.surface: Instructions on undoing a tie that Tim has tied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take off' means mimic; the definition is an imperative, an order to mimic.
explanation.definitionFit: To take off someone is to mimic them, so the command form tells you to copy.

clue.text: The most important course at sea

definitions.text: The most important course at sea

parts.words: The most important course at sea
parts.note: the chief course of a meal, with a nod to 'the ...' meaning the sea, so it sounds like a ship's route

explanation.surface: A ship's principal route across the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course at sea' suggests navigation, but it is a course of a meal; 'the main' is a poetic word for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal course of a meal is its centrepiece plate.

clue.text: Orsino's noted food of love

parts.note: Duke Orsino opens Twelfth Night with 'If ... be the food of love, play on'; 'noted' hints at ... notes

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character's famous line about what nourishes love.
explanation.walkthrough: Orsino is the duke in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night. 'noted' means famous and also made of notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's lovesick duke calls melody the food of love in his opening speech.

clue.text: The routine that makes physician sick

parts.note: Dr is short for doctor, a physician
sick means ill

explanation.surface: A procedure that turns doctors' stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that makes' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeated practice of fixed exercises, as on the parade ground, is a set routine.

clue.text: See 21
No turn-up for you and me it's hard to bear

indicators.note: in a down clue a turn-up flips the word upward, so it is read backwards

parts.note: you and me together are us

explanation.surface: No surprise for us: it's a heavy burden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn-up' (a surprise) turns NO up into ON in this down light; 'for' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: A burden or responsibility is a weight to carry.

clue.text: Some votes partly delay estimates

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Votes that hold up budget estimates.
explanation.definitionFit: Votes in favour in Parliament are counted as the yes side of a division.

clue.text: Firm stem

definitions.meaning: to stop a flow, especially of blood

explanation.surface: A sturdy plant stalk.
explanation.definitionFit: A loyal supporter is steadfast, and stopping a flow of blood is checking it.

clue.text: Wilful manner having drawback

parts.note: a way is a manner

indicators.note: back says the word draw is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A headstrong manner that has its downside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drawback' looks like one word meaning a disadvantage, but splits into 'draw' and the reversal signal 'back', giving WARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A headstrong person is self-willed and hard to control.

clue.text: Drops in and makes an appeal

explanation.surface: Someone visiting to make a plea.
explanation.definitionFit: Visiting someone briefly and formally requesting something both use the same phrasal verb.

clue.text: They may flock from Ephesus but no, we object

indicators.note: from says the letters are drawn out of the place name and formed into something new

parts.note: as an object pronoun, we becomes us

explanation.surface: A complaint from the people of an ancient city about crowds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but no' tells you to remove US from EPHESUS, leaving EPHES, which 'from' reworks into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Animals that gather in flocks include woolly grazing livestock.
